title: Gap-junction closure in transformation is a positive feedback loop of isolation

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Gap-junction closure in transformation is a positive feedback loop of isolation

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Cells may physiologically disconnect from the tissue network (e.g. closing gap junctions under prolonged stress), and each reduction in connectivity makes local computation easier and further gap-junction closure more likely, a positive feedback loop of dissociation that makes tissue-level goals ever harder to achieve; Levin presents this as consistent with gap-junction closure in early transformation and with tumours induced by non-carcinogenic geometric barriers.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Cancer and the Scaling of the Self

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Each reduction in physiological connectivity makes it easier for cells to perform computations at the local level. This makes it easier for cells to close off gap junctions even more, driving a positive feedback loop—a cycle of dissociation and isolation that makes it ever harder to achieve large‐scale cell collective goals (maintaining complex anatomical structure).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Cancer and the Scaling of the Self”. Scope: Early carcinogenic transformation in animal tissues

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Connectivity and transformation are measurable, and public cancer profiles can test associations. The proposed temporal self-reinforcement and tissue-goal interpretation need functional longitudinal data not broadly available.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In longitudinal transformation data, quantify gap-junction coupling, local-state autonomy and malignancy, testing whether an initial coupling decrease predicts further closure and whether restoring coupling interrupts progression. A self-amplifying temporal relation supports the feedback mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Connexin expression is an imperfect proxy for functional coupling.

Geometric-barrier evidence may not share the same mechanism.

Cross-sectional tumours cannot establish positive feedback.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.4

operationalizability: 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cancer genomics can show whether gap-junction transcripts are lower in tumors, which is a weak correlate of the isolation half of the claim. The claim's distinctive content is a positive feedback loop in which each loss of coupling makes the next loss more likely, and a one-time expression matrix cannot test that sequence. The feedback mechanism remains only partly addressable with public data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In early transformation, measure gap-junction coupling over time and test whether an experimental reduction in coupling raises the probability of further uncoupling and of local, rather than tissue-scale, growth control. A rising hazard of further closure after partial uncoupling would support the feedback claim; independent closures, or no link to loss of tissue-level anatomy, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A cross-sectional expression difference cannot show positive feedback.

Geometric-barrier tumor experiments are not in cancer genomics archives.

Expression of junction genes is not junction permeability, and tumors are sampled once.
